title: Identification of M-theory's fundamental degrees of freedom and a test of whether it describes nature

concept.text: Strings 2000 problem 7 (proposed by Louise Dolan, Annamaria Sinkovics, and Billy and Linda Rose): what are the fundamental degrees of freedom of M-theory, the theory whose low-energy limit is eleven-dimensional supergravity and which subsumes the five consistent superstring theories, and does the theory describe Nature? Sources given: https://preskill.caltech.edu/millennium.html ; https://aip.brightspotcdn.com/PTO.v54.i10.14_2.online.pdf ; https://x.com/martinmbauer/status/1779906631003697211.

change_log.change: Added by hand to PHY on 2026-11-15.
change_log.reason: One of the ten Physics Problems for the Next Millennium chosen at the Strings 2000 conference (University of Michigan) by a panel of Michael Duff, David Gross and Edward Witten; added at the owner's request, November 14, 2026.

page.title: Nonperturbative formulation and empirical test of M-theory
page.definition: A nonperturbative formulation specifies M-theory’s quantum variables and their dynamics without assuming weak string interactions. It recovers eleven-dimensional supergravity at low energies and the five superstring theories in their respective limits. The BFSS matrix model proposes such dynamics for scattering in flat eleven-dimensional spacetime. The empirical test requires a vacuum, or stable or metastable ground state, with four extended spacetime dimensions and a measurable prediction that distinguishes it from competing models.

goal.need: At the earliest times in the universe, calculations of how matter behaved require a quantum treatment of gravity. The reduced Planck energy is roughly 14 orders of magnitude above collision energies at the Large Hadron Collider. Weak-coupling calculations also lose control in the regime where an eleventh dimension emerges. If a four-dimensional vacuum relates that microscopic physics to a measurable particle mass, collider experiments could test physics at otherwise inaccessible energies. The inference depends on the vacuum and its particle content.

statements.body: Strings 2000 selection panel (Michael Duff, David Gross and Edward Witten)
statements.context: Problem 7 of Physics Problems for the Next Millennium pairs this question with identifying M-theory’s fundamental degrees of freedom. The conference credits Louise Dolan, Annamaria Sinkovics, Billy Rose and Linda Rose with the problem.

statements.quote: Clearly, this is a direction to be pursued.
statements.context: In Connecting Quarks with the Cosmos, the Council used “string theory” to include M-theory. It endorsed work on quantum corrections to gravity and on information in black-hole radiation. It also observed that different four-dimensional solutions gave different particles and interactions.

completion.title: A microscopic formulation of M-theory passes a discriminating empirical test.
completion.criterion: A formulation specifies fundamental quantum variables and dynamics and recovers eleven-dimensional supergravity and the five superstring limits. For a specified four-dimensional vacuum, it predicts a numerical observable beyond the data used to choose or fit that vacuum. An independent measurement agrees within the stated theoretical and experimental uncertainties and distinguishes the prediction from specified competing descriptions under the experiment’s published decision criterion. Agreement tests the formulation together with the chosen vacuum.
completion.set_by: Atlas fallback, interpreting the two parts of Strings 2000 problem 7.
completion.basis: Strings 2000 problem 7 asks for both microscopic variables and a connection to nature. Searches of that list, National Research Council reports, the BFSS proposal, matrix-theory reviews and string-phenomenology papers found no joint completion criterion or M-theory-wide experimental significance threshold. This fallback combines the two requested outcomes. A successful test of one vacuum would support that model; it would not establish that M-theory is the unique description of nature.

milestones.title: Matrix quantum mechanics reproduces the two-loop v⁶/r¹⁴ graviton interaction from supergravity.
milestones.criterion: For two gravitons moving slowly at large separation with zero longitudinal momentum transfer, match the coefficient of v⁶/r¹⁴ in the two-loop matrix effective action to the coefficient in eleven-dimensional supergravity, including its normalization. Here v is the relative transverse speed and r is the separation.
milestones.set_by: The matrix-theory scattering consistency test introduced by BFSS and extended to two loops by Becker, Becker, Polchinski and Tseytlin. This test concerns the flat-space matrix-model proposal.
milestones.threshold_quote: Low energy supergravity predicts the coefficient of the $v^6/r^{14}$ term, a two-loop effect, in agreement with explicit matrix model calculation.

milestones.title: BFSS scattering amplitudes obey eleven-dimensional Lorentz symmetry as matrix size tends to infinity.
milestones.criterion: Establish the full eleven-dimensional Lorentz symmetry of quantum scattering amplitudes in the BFSS matrix model as the matrix size N tends to infinity. This includes boosts along the longitudinal direction and Lorentz transformations that rotate the lightlike surface on which the theory is quantized.
milestones.set_by: BFSS, section 8 of their matrix-model proposal; subsequently investigated by Tropper and Wang. The published criterion was written for the BFSS model.
milestones.threshold_quote: It is clearly important to determine if the matrix model satisfies the angular conditions in the large N limit.

milestones.title: An M-theory compactification yields three chiral families and the Standard Model gauge group.
milestones.criterion: Derive from an M-theory compactification a four-dimensional effective theory with three chiral families of quarks and leptons coupled to the Standard Model gauge group SU(3)C × SU(2)L × U(1)Y. Chirality here means that the left- and right-handed fields transform differently under the weak interaction.
milestones.set_by: The three-family Standard Model spectrum used in particle-physics model building, implemented by Donagi, Ovrut, Pantev and Waldram. Their published construction concerns heterotic M-theory.
milestones.threshold_quote: three families of chiral quarks and leptons coupled to the gauge group $SU(3)_C\times SU(2)_{L}\times U(1)_{Y}$.

milestones.title: One microscopic quantum formulation yields eleven-dimensional supergravity and all five superstring limits.
milestones.criterion: Specify the fundamental quantum variables and dynamics without relying on a weak-coupling expansion. From that formulation, derive eleven-dimensional supergravity at low energies and recover each of the five consistent ten-dimensional superstring theories in its appropriate limit.
milestones.set_by: Atlas fallback. No common external acceptance test specifies how to establish one microscopic formulation across all five string limits.

milestones.title: A four-dimensional M-theory vacuum predicts an experimental signature beyond fitted observations.
milestones.criterion: For a specified four-dimensional M-theory vacuum, identify the observations used to select the vacuum or fix its parameters. Derive an experimentally accessible signature beyond those inputs.
milestones.set_by: The string-phenomenology progression articulated by Cleaver and colleagues in their abstract and introduction. Their worked example concerns heterotic strings; Kane and Acharya, Kane and Kumar apply vacuum-based prediction to M-theory.
milestones.threshold_quote: The subsequent goal is to extract potential signatures beyond the observable data.

milestones.title: Matrix quantum mechanics reproduces the one-loop v⁴/r⁷ interaction from single-graviton exchange.
milestones.criterion: For two gravitons moving slowly at large separation with zero longitudinal momentum transfer, match the coefficient of the spin-independent v⁴/r⁷ term in the one-loop matrix effective action to single-graviton exchange in eleven-dimensional supergravity. Here v is the relative transverse speed and r is the separation.
milestones.set_by: Banks, Fischler, Shenker and Susskind’s matrix-model scattering test, evaluated at one loop by Katrin Becker and Melanie Becker.
milestones.threshold_quote: At one-loop we obtain the well known result for the leading order of the effective potential $V_{eff}\sim v^4/r^7$

not_found: No laboratory demonstration of M-theory’s fundamental degrees of freedom was found.

results.finding: For two gravitons, the two-loop matrix calculation matches the supergravity v⁶/r¹⁴ prefactor of 225/64 in the large-source limit.
results.detail: The comparison holds at fixed longitudinal momenta and uses a classical source graviton and a straight-line probe. The prefactor multiplies N₁²N₂/(R⁵ M¹⁸).
results.quote:
Low energy supergravity predicts the co eﬃcient
of the v6/r14 term, a two-loop eﬀect, in agreement with explicit matrix
model calculation.

results.finding: For two D0-brane clusters, supersymmetry fixes the two-loop v⁶ coefficient in terms of lower-derivative terms.
results.detail: The r⁻²² result applies to the twelve-fermion partner of the bosonic interaction.
results.quote:
Even
the numerical coeﬃcient of the v6 term is ﬁxed in terms of lower derivative terms in the
eﬀective action.

results.finding: For BFSS D0-brane bound-state scattering at arbitrary multiplicity, the soft-theorem Ward identities imply 11-dimensional Lorentz symmetry as N tends to infinity.
results.detail: Appendix A checks the leading soft factor via the nonrelativistic limit of type IIA D0-brane scattering. The subleading factor is needed for the two Lorentz Ward identities that extend the manifest BFSS symmetries.
results.quote:
BFSS scattering amplitudes exhibit the full 11d Poincaré symmetry of M-theory which emerges only in the large
N

results.finding: Large-N BFSS scattering has eleven-dimensional Lorentz symmetry for general amplitudes with 4 external particles, assuming a smooth limit.
results.detail: The derivation keeps the soft graviton’s longitudinal momentum nonzero before taking the soft limit. This gives the longitudinal-momentum derivatives in the Lorentz generators that mix the lightlike direction with other directions.
results.quote:
The subleading soft theorem implies the amplitude is Lorentz symmetric. This is argued
for general four point amplitudes, but only for restricted kinematics for five and higher
point amplitudes.

results.finding: Five candidate heterotic M-theory bundle classes give three chiral quark and lepton families with the Standard Model gauge group if the bundles descend.
results.detail: The authors defer the construction of exactly invariant bundles. They explicitly note that non-invariant bundles can have invariant Chern classes, so the computed data alone cannot establish descent.
results.quote:
that contain three familie s of chiral quarks and leptons
coupled to the gauge group SU (3)C×SU (2)L×U (1)Y.

results.finding: One family of heterotic M-theory compactifications yields three chiral quark and lepton families with the Standard Model gauge group.
results.quote:
We obtain three families of
quark and lepton superﬁelds, one copy of the gauge connectio ns, and no exotic matter.

results.finding: G₂-MSSM Higgs mass prediction across three gravitino-mass benchmarks: 122–129 GeV.
results.detail: Big-bang nucleosynthesis constrains the lower gravitino mass. The observed electroweak scale constrains the Higgs-sector parameters, and tan β remains a scan parameter.

results.finding: One G₂-MSSM benchmark predicts a gluino mass of about 1.5 TeV.
results.detail: The benchmark assumes A2/Q = 1. Unknown ultraviolet threshold corrections broaden the predicted gluino mass to 1–2 TeV.
results.quote:
The gluino mass is predicted to be about 1.5
TeV.

results.finding: For two Kaluza–Klein gravitons, the one-loop matrix and single-graviton exchange v⁴/r⁷ coefficients agree at 15/16 in units of N₁N₂/(R³M⁹).
results.detail: Section 4 compares the two Lagrangians directly after converting the matrix result to Minkowski signature and common units.
results.quote:
reproduce exactly the same phase shifts as those of Matrix theory (4.3) and (4.4), since the
integrands in these expressions are identical with the correspond ing eﬀective Lagrangians
of supergravity.

results.finding: For two D0-branes, the two-loop matrix effective action reproduces the prior SU(2) result after a factor-of-2 normalization adjustment.
results.detail: The factor of 2 converts between matrix-model conventions for the SU(2) generators.
results.quote:
The two-loop contributions to the eﬀective
action are proportional to g2, which means that the results in this paper must be divided
by a factor of 2 for comparison with the results in [13].

results.finding: Large-N BFSS effective-theory amplitudes with one soft graviton and n hard states factorize through subleading order O(N⁰).
results.detail: The pairwise effective action has zero longitudinal momentum transfer, which the authors treat as negligible for soft emission or absorption. The symmetry conclusion is limited to the regime of the effective theory.
results.quote:
their
correlation functions exhibit soft factorization at both leading and subleading orders.

results.finding: BFSS n-point single-minus graviton amplitudes match 11-dimensional supergravity exactly in one decay chamber, even at finite matrix ranks.
results.detail: The calculation assumes that string-web wall-crossing formulas apply to the matrix-string field theory and uses primitive charge vectors.
results.quote: Under these explicit assumptions, the resulting agreement is exact in the stated chamber.

results.finding: One heterotic M-theory compactification model yields 3 chiral quark and lepton families with the Standard Model gauge group after B−L breaking.
results.detail: The compactification initially gives an extra U(1)B−L. With soft supersymmetry breaking and selected initial parameters, the authors find a stable local minimum that breaks this extra factor above the electroweak scale.
results.quote:
Vacuum (19) spontaneously breaks the gauged B-L symmetry giving the B-L
vector boson a mass,

results.finding: A local G₂ model with one deformed E8 singularity yields three chiral quark and lepton families with Standard Model charges.
results.detail: The authors derive masses for two extra U(1) gauge bosons through anomaly cancellation and propose electroweak Higgs VEVs to give mass to the third.
results.quote:
M-theory compactified on a G2 manifold with resolved E8 singularities realizes four-dimensional
N ¼ 1 supersymmetric gauge theories coupled to gravity with three families of Standard Model fermions.

results.finding: For BFSS matrix size N = 2, the localized partition function scales as p², matching the eleven-dimensional three-graviton amplitude’s relative-momentum dependence.
results.detail: The calculation fixes the total light-cone momentum through discrete light-cone quantization. The comparison assumes that the flat-space three-point amplitude has the same momentum dependence at finite N. The calculation leaves the overall normalization undetermined.
results.quote:
We find that the result correctly reproduces the expected
momentum dependence of the three point amplitude.

results.finding: Matrix string theory recovers the free spectrum of 1 of 5 ten-dimensional superstring theories, type IIA, in the large-N infrared limit.
results.detail: N is the gauge-group rank, taken to infinity. The spectrum follows from the symmetric-product orbifold, and the leading interaction follows from a twist operator. The supplied preprint mentions independent overlap without specifying which results were independently obtained.
results.quote:
We have seen that the super-Yang-Mills model in the IR limit g ives the free light-cone
quantization of the type IIA string in terms of an orbifold si gma model

results.finding: The Type IIB matrix limit recovers O(8) transverse rotational symmetry in a theoretical derivation.
results.detail: The symmetry argument assumes Yang–Mills S-duality and identifies momentum in the emergent direction with magnetic flux. Establishing the symmetry tests the Type IIB limit without deriving its full dynamics.
results.quote:
In fact, the enti re rotational O(8) symmetry
then follows.

results.finding: The O(N) D-string gauge theory gives discrete light-cone matrix descriptions of 3 superstring theories.
results.detail: N labels a gauge-rank sector. For type I, the paper recovers the massless spectrum in the N=1 sector and leaves agreement with the full perturbative theory open.
results.quote:
We have seen how the two Heterotic strings have a matrix model description as a
1+1 dimensional O(N) gauge theory.

results.finding: The heterotic M-theory B−L MSSM inflation model predicts r ≃ 0.00334 in a study that scanned 10 million soft-parameter points.
results.detail: The tensor-to-scalar ratio is a CMB observable derived from the potential shape. The scan tests low-energy viability at the CMB-normalized mass scale. The authors also identify other supergravity models with the same soft-term potential.

results.finding: Across 9,727 viable B−L MSSM parameter points with Wino LSPs, most charged–neutral Wino mass splittings are below 200 MeV, favoring observable R-parity-violating decays of both states.
results.detail: The LHC prediction is conditional on sufficiently light Winos and is calculated at leading order across viable effective-theory spectra.
results.quote: Note that most mass splittings are ≲ 200 MeV .
